title: Cycle Pivot Windows: time-boxed staff rotations and deterministic scope offboarding
creator: Priya Menon
description: Problem: During mid-cycle surges we repeatedly scramble staffing and make ad-hoc scope cuts, causing uneven velocity and unclear ownership. Objective: Define a lightweight, repeatable Cycle Pivot Windows framework that prescribes (1) how to rotate staff into surge lanes via time-boxed micro-rotations, (2) criteria for deterministic scope offboarding (what gets cut and how), and (3) signals and dashboards to automate decision triggers. Goals: reduce mid-cycle scope churn by 50%, reduce cross-team rework on critical path features, and ensure decision traceability for leadership and customers. Success metrics: percent of scope changes executed via the Pivot Windows process, median time-to-recover planner alignment after a surge, NPS from impacted PM/Eng leads. Scope: this playbook covers PM and Eng staffing, design touchpoints, and runbook templates for cycle weeks 1-6. It does NOT include hiring or long-term resourcing changes (out of scope).
acceptance_criteria: Final playbook published in Confluence with copy + templates
Two simulated pivots run in our staging cycle with post-mortem notes
Dashboard tile added to CycleFlow showing pivot triggers and current pivot state
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng leads, Design lead, and Revenue ops
Rollout guide and 30-minute onboarding for cycle leads created
decisions: Adopt 7-day Pivot Window (default) with optional 3-day micro-window for critical hotfix lanes
Rotation unit = 1 engineer + 50% of a cross-functional PM/design time; budgeted as temporary reallocate, not hire
Deterministic offboarding uses the Impact-Complexity matrix with pre-assigned tie-breakers (product priority -> customer concentration -> technical unblockability)
Pivot initiation triggers: sustained >20% velocity delta on critical path OR P1 incident that blocks roadmap work for >8 hours
Use CycleFlow dashboard and PagerDuty alerts (integration ticket ENG-74321) as canonical signals; manual override requires written justification
